sections.heading: What the checklist is
paragraphs: It is a one-page monthly cleaning record for an office, an ODC floor or any workspace. Tasks run down the left side, the days of the month run across, and each box is ticked when the job is done.
Two rows at the bottom let the cleaner and the supervisor sign off each day. It is drawn in your browser, and nothing you type is uploaded.

sections.heading: Why a written record helps
paragraphs: Cleaning is easy to notice when it is missed and hard to prove when it is done. A sheet on the wall shows what was done each day, supports the contractor when work is complete and gives the facility manager something to point to when it is not.
It also sets expectations clearly for a new cleaner: the tasks are written down, not remembered.

sections.heading: Setting it up
paragraphs: Walk the floor once and list every recurring job. Put the daily jobs on this sheet, and keep the monthly and yearly ones for the weekly schedule and the deep cleaning planner. Fix the sheet at a place the cleaner passes each day, with a pen on a string.
Review it at the end of the month with the housekeeping team and adjust the tasks that are missed or not needed.

sections.heading: What the chart is
paragraphs: It is a monthly sheet for the cleaning of a washroom. Tasks are listed down the side, each day of the month has a column, and a box is ticked when a task is done.
You can name the washroom, change the tasks and print sheets for as many washrooms as you have. It is drawn in your browser.

sections.heading: Why keep one
paragraphs: A washroom is the first place people judge a building. A chart on the door shows staff and visitors that the place is cared for, and shows the supervisor which days a task was skipped.
It also makes the contractor's work easy to review at the end of the month.

sections.heading: Using it
paragraphs: Fix the chart on the inside of the door or on a service cupboard. The cleaner ticks each task as it is done, and the supervisor does a quick check. Combine it with the hourly round sheet if the washroom needs checks during the day.
Replace the sheet at the start of each month, and keep the old ones with the housekeeping records.

sections.heading: What the log is
paragraphs: It is a monthly sheet for the daily cleaning of a lift. Tasks run down the side, the days of the month run across, and a box is ticked when each job is done.
You can name the lift, change the tasks and print one sheet for each lift. It is drawn in your browser.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: In a residential society or an office building the lifts are among the most used spaces. A short daily routine keeps them presentable, and a log keeps the routine honest.
It is also something a committee or a facility manager can show when residents or tenants ask what is being done.

sections.heading: Using the log
paragraphs: Put the daily jobs here, such as the floor, mirror and buttons, and add the weekly jobs to the weekly cleaning schedule. Technical checks are a different record and are kept by the lift company.
At the end of the month, file the sheet and print a new one.

sections.heading: What the checklist is
paragraphs: It is a monthly sheet for the cleaning of a guest room, hostel room or PG room. Tasks run down the left side, days run across, and a box is ticked when a job is done.
It has two sign-off rows for the housekeeper and the supervisor. The sheet is drawn in your browser, and nothing you type is uploaded.

sections.heading: Why use one
paragraphs: Rooms that are cleaned to the same routine every time get fewer complaints. A checklist in the housekeeping cupboard or on the trolley is a reminder for staff and a record for the manager.
For hostels and PGs it also settles the question of when a room was last cleaned.

sections.heading: Setting it up
paragraphs: List the tasks in the order the housekeeper does them, from the bed to the bathroom, so the sheet matches the routine. Keep the daily list short, and put weekly and monthly tasks in the weekly schedule and the deep cleaning planner.
File the sheets for each room at the end of the month.

sections.heading: What the checklist is
paragraphs: It is a monthly sheet for the cleaning of a pantry, tea station, canteen or kitchen. Tasks are listed down the side, the days of the month run across, and each box is ticked when a job is done.
There are two sign-off rows at the bottom for the cleaner and the supervisor. It is drawn in your browser.

sections.heading: Why keep it
paragraphs: Shared kitchens drift. Cups pile up, the fridge fills with old food, and the sink is nobody's job. A checklist makes the job someone's, and the signature shows whose.
It also gives the office manager a calm answer when someone complains about the pantry.

sections.heading: Using it
paragraphs: Write the tasks in the order the cleaner works. Keep daily jobs on this sheet. Put the monthly jobs, like defrosting the fridge or cleaning the chimney, on the deep cleaning planner.
Review the sheet at month end and take out tasks that never get done or add ones that are always missing.

sections.heading: What the checklist is
paragraphs: It is a monthly record of the daily cleaning of a society's common areas. Tasks are listed down the left, the days of the month run across, and a box is ticked each time a job is done.
Two rows at the bottom let the housekeeping staff and the supervisor sign off the day. It is drawn in your browser, and nothing you type is uploaded.

sections.heading: Why it helps a committee
paragraphs: Residents notice dirt and rarely notice cleaning. A visible daily record lets the committee answer complaints with facts, supports the contractor when work is done properly and gives the facility manager a way to follow up on gaps.
It also makes handover easy when a new staff member or a new contractor starts.

sections.heading: Setting it up
paragraphs: Walk the premises with the supervisor and list the tasks for each area, in the order the staff do them. Print a sheet for each tower or block, and put each on the notice board near the area it covers.
Review it each month at the committee meeting and keep the old sheets with the society's records.

sections.heading: What the schedule is
paragraphs: It is a one-page weekly roster for housekeeping. Areas run down the left side, the days of the week run across, and the last columns hold the frequency, the person assigned and the supervisor's sign.
The list starts with common areas of a society and can be edited for an office or any other site. It is drawn in your browser.

sections.heading: Why a schedule matters
paragraphs: Without a schedule, cleaning goes to whatever is noticed. With one, every area has a day, every day has a person, and the supervisor can check that the plan is being followed.
It also helps with changes: if a staff member is absent, the roster shows what needs covering.

sections.heading: Using it with the daily sheets
paragraphs: Fill in the roster at the start of the week, and pin it where the staff and supervisor see it. Use the daily checklist to record what was actually done. Keep each week's roster so that you can see how the plan changed over time.
Review it monthly and adjust days and assignments as the site changes.

sections.heading: What the round sheet is
paragraphs: It is a daily page for washroom and area checks. Areas run down the left side, the times of the rounds run across, and the cleaner writes initials in the box at each round.
You choose the time of the first round, the gap between rounds and the number of rounds, and print as many days as you need. It is drawn in your browser.

sections.heading: Why use one
paragraphs: Busy washrooms in offices, malls, schools and public buildings need checks through the day, and a sheet on the door shows that they happen. Visitors see the check, and supervisors can see gaps.
The remarks and supervisor sign turn a simple tick sheet into a short daily report.

sections.heading: Using it
paragraphs: Fix the sheet on the washroom door or on the cleaner's trolley. Set the rounds to match the shift, and keep the interval short for the busiest hours. At the end of the day, the supervisor signs and files it.
Keep a month of sheets together. A repeating problem, like a tap that is always leaking, is easier to spot when the notes are in one place.

sections.heading: What the record is
paragraphs: It is a landscape table for logging periodic cleaning and service jobs. Each row is one job, with the date, the area or item, the work done, who did it, when it is next due and who checked it.
The title is yours to type, so one sheet design serves for tanks, pest control and servicing. It is drawn in your browser.

sections.heading: Why keep a record
paragraphs: Periodic jobs are the ones that get forgotten. A written record with a next due date turns a vague memory into a plan, and it protects a society or business by showing that the work was done.
It is also useful when a contractor or a new committee takes over.

sections.heading: Using it well
paragraphs: Fill in the row on the day of the work, with the contractor present if you can. Write the next due date in the Next due column and copy it to a calendar or phone reminder. Keep the contractor's paperwork with the sheet.
Leave the cleaning method and any chemicals to the licensed contractor, and follow your local rules.

sections.heading: What the planner is
paragraphs: It is a yearly grid for planning the big cleaning jobs. Jobs are listed down the left side and the twelve months run across the page, with a Done by column at the end.
You can edit the list of jobs, choose the first month and the year, and print it in landscape. It is drawn in your browser.

sections.heading: Why plan the year
paragraphs: Big jobs have to be booked: contractors need notice, some work needs the building empty, and some jobs are best done in a particular season. A planner on the wall spreads the work across the year and avoids a rush.
It also lets a manager or committee see at a glance what is due this month.

sections.heading: Using it
paragraphs: Sit down once a year with the contractors and your records and mark when each job will happen. Put the planner where the facility team sees it, and copy the dates to a calendar.
At the end of the year, use it to see what was done, what was missed and what to change for the next one.
